newsitem.title: UK: British Treasury may contract out economic forecasting.
newsitem.headline: British Treasury may contract out economic forecasting.

text.p: The British Treasury said on Tuesday it is to investigate the feasibility of contracting out its economic forecasting to an independent company.
"To carry this forward, the Treasury will shortly be appointing a consultant to advise on the feasibility and scope of a market test," it said in a statement.
The consultant will look at the feasibility of contracting out the forecasting of the key econommic aggregates, and the forecasting and monitoring of public finances.
"If the consultant's report found a market test would be feasible, the Treasury expects to issue a formal contract specification in the late spring or early summer," it added.
The study is expected to last around three months.
Treasury staff would be able to mount an in-house bid if the contracting out goes ahead.

"The aim would be to complete negotiations with potential service providers in time for the successful bidder to take over responsibility for the contracted services from the end of 1997," the Treasury said.

Major independent forecasting bodies, such as the National Institute of Economic and Social Research or the London Business School, could be the type of firm expected to submit bids if the contracting out goes ahead.
The government has introduced competition into the provision of services across a range of departments.
